title: Values re-set on the 2026-27 roll for buildings behind City deals
question: Which deal buildings did the Assessor revalue on the new roll, beyond the 2% yearly rise the law allows without a sale or new work?
finding: 20 deal parcels moved more than 3% and more than $250,000 between the 2025-26 and 2026-27 rolls: 10 up, 10 down. Largest rise: 1380 Howard Street; 1380 Howard ($5,397,142 to $28,298,880). 758 Pacific Avenue, which the Board approved buying in 2026 (no deed to the City is on the recorder's index saved in November 2026) after a sale dated 8 August 2023 that set no new value on four rolls, is now carried at $2,080,800 (from $805,696); the 2026-27 roll value is 96% of it.
how: Land plus improvement value on the 2025-26 and 2026-27 workbooks for each deal parcel; a change beyond 3% and $250,000 is listed. The sale date is the latest one either roll carries from 2025 on. Prices are those the parcels screen read from Board file titles.
limits: A value rises beyond 2% only after a change in ownership or new construction, and falls after a decline-in-value review, a lot split or demolition; which of these happened is not on the roll. Tax-credit buildings and City-owned land can be revalued when a partnership is restructured or a ground lease is signed. No price or owner is on the roll. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
